messages.author: 28471c1900f3aa84
messages.subject: Half-sib design and genotype coding
parts:
Hi all,

I'm working with a half-sib cross data for expression qtl mapping
(normally distributed trait). I would want to use Rqtl but I'm very
new in the field of mapping and qtl's. And related to that I have a
couple of questions.

1. Related to the conversion of genotypes (microsats) to coding
explained in the read.cross. I came across to post by Amanda K and
what she describes is similar to what I have going on in my data set.
Are there any scripts/programs available which could be used for doing
the conversion of alleles to the equivalent Rqtl codes? I've got the
genotype information for parents and offspring.

2. In the FAQ on the homepage it is stated that data half-sib families
cannot be analyzed. Is it truly this strict? I was just thinking that
since the genotype information is coded the inherent half-sib
structure is diluted? Please, correct me if I'm wrong?

I would really appreciate it if somenone could give an answer to me.
I'm also wellcome to any suggestions for which statistical models
would be suitable to my type of data. Thanks,
Heidi

R/qtl is largely for the analysis of crosses based on inbred lines. It contains no code for dealing with groups of half-sib families.

karl
